subject_location.head_commit: bdc4c01 'WF-044: emit a webhook out of the CRM when a deal stage changes'

A_plugin_shaped_and_buildable.does: Package surface. Re-exports the domain's public names.

The researched vocabulary as data: POST and GET, the HTTPS-only URL rule, three authentication types, two body modes, three objects, two permissions, the 1000-per-app cap, and the outcome and reason vocabulary. Every constant quotes the sentence in the research that makes it part of the specification. Served at GET /api/wf-044/vocabulary so the editor can never disagree with the validator.

One error hierarchy under WebhookError, each carrying its own code and HTTP status, so the feature registers a single EXCEPTION_HANDLERS entry for the whole hierarchy. 401 for a request that failed authentication, 403 for a missing permission, 409 for a conflict with live state.

The three researched authentication methods and nothing else: HMAC-SHA256 request signature with a HubSpot App ID, an API key in a header or a query parameter, and 'Bearer [YOUR_TOKEN]'. Constant-time comparison, a 300 second replay window compared as a signed distance in either direction, and a GET signs an empty body. The module states at the top that the signature scheme is the one thing the workflow's three sources do not publish.

The versioned payload contract, and the one rule that reads both researched body shapes: 'Include all [object] properties' nests under 'properties', 'Customize request body' is a flat key table. Everything not a reserved control key is kept verbatim as a property.

WebhookEngine over a RecordStore: the whole second half of the researched flow. Register, amend, publish, unpublish, add and retire automations, receive a signed POST or GET, resolve the record, update the deal panel, notify the rep, and read the delivery log. One inbound endpoint per room and any number of automations aimed at it. The 1000-per-app cap is counted across rooms because the source counts per app. A retry is counted on the delivery that was kept, not stored twice. source= is a required keyword on every writing method, so the audit row cannot name a path the app does not serve.

Twelve judgement calls this build rests on, each named, traceable to what the research does and does not say, bounded by a value, and served at GET /api/wf-044/inferences. Includes a not-built entry recording that Salesforce outbound messages and Dataverse Service Bus are unsourced and so not modelled.

The feature module. Exports FEATURE with id 'wf-044-emit-a-webhook-out-of-the-crm-when-a-d' and ticket 'WF-044', a router with the unique prefix /api/wf-044, EXCEPTION_HANDLERS mapping WebhookError, and seed(db, context). 20 routes, all room-scoped, with the contract version in the path. Every route passes source=f'{router.prefix}...' and nothing is interpolated from a concrete id. The webhook route reads await request.body() and hands the raw text on, because a signature covers the exact bytes sent. Imports only from dsr.deps, never from dsr.api.

267 tests. Not weakened: they assert the researched sentences, drive the mounted routes through TestClient rather than calling handlers, check that every audit source names a route the host reports, assert the module never imports dsr.api, assert the package never opens the database, assert a delivery rolls back whole, and assert the seed produces the states that are not successes.

The frontend registration: a default-export descriptor with id, label, icon, iconPath, order and Component. The id matches FEATURE['id'] exactly. Nothing in App.jsx, main.jsx or lib/features.js learns the feature's name.

The feature's own API calls on the shared apiRequest, with every write carrying the researched permissions string. Deliberately has no deliver call: the inbound endpoint is something the CRM posts to, not something a browser invokes by hand.

Local presentation pieces built inside the feature folder because ui.jsx is shared: a copyable field, a definition list, a research note, and four glyphs passed to <Icon path=...> rather than added to the shared PATHS map.

The page. Six tabs following the researched flow: Endpoint, Automations, Deliveries, Deal panel, Rep, Decisions. Semantic tokens only, no raw hex, min-h-11 touch targets, focus-visible rings, no emoji as icons, and it deliberately offers no 'test' button because the researched Test control is a CRM-side control, so the room shows the bytes it expects and says so.

why_not_B_and_why_not_C.B: The one-commit diff against its own merge base touches none of the eleven shared files. It does not edit backend/dsr/api.py, deps.py, store.py, db/audited.py or backend/seed.py, and it does not edit frontend/src/App.jsx, main.jsx, lib/api.js, lib/features.js, components/ui.jsx or vite.config.js. It adds files and nothing else.
why_not_B_and_why_not_C.C: Main has no equivalent under any path. git ls-tree over origin/main shows no backend/dsr/crm_outbound_webhooks, no wf044 feature module in backend/dsr/features, and no wf-044 folder in frontend/src/features. The only match for 'outbound_webhook' on main is one line in backend/dsr/crm_workflows/inferences.py recording that the path was 'not built'.

That is a bookkeeping consequence, not a reason to refuse a good plugin, and it is recorded so the decision is made with it in view.
